name: fib
axis: naive binary (non-tail) recursion — raw call/return overhead with a near-empty body
notes: fib(42) = ~866M calls (2*F(43)-1). Body is one compare + one add, so >90% of the time is call/return. Sized so the slowest non-Python runtime (deno) lands ~1.9s. Python gets n=35 (~123x less work) because CPython at n=42 would be ~85s. Scale-verified against the EXACT call-count ratio rather than 2N: fib(40)/fib(42) work ratio is 0.382 (F(41)/F(43)); measured rust 0.375, deno 0.397, vl 0.435 — no runtime folded the recursion. Measured (min-of-3, taskset -c 6, quiet machine): rust 0.631s, vl 0.914s, deno 1.877s, python(n=35) 0.682s. VL is 2.05x FASTER than deno and 1.45x slower than rust — a good result for this axis; no hand-optimized variant is possible or needed.

startupBaselineSeconds._measured: min-of-10, empty program, taskset -c 6, contended 24-core i9-12900KF

compileTime._note: compile time, measured separately and never inside an execution number

consolidatedRun._method: single interleaved pass over ALL 8 recursion benchmarks, min-of-3, taskset -c 6, per-runtime empty-program startup subtracted, machine contended by other agents (loadavg ~10) so read the RATIOS not the absolutes
